prompt: On a humid summer evening, the sky is clear and the air is still. The air stays near 18 °C all night, but the grass loses heat and becomes a few degrees colder than the air around it. What will most likely be found on the grass by dawn?
choices: A dry surface, as the cool air draws water out of grass.
Water droplets that condensed from vapor in the humid air.
Frost, because the grass drops below the freezing point of water.
Raindrops from clouds too thin to see in the dark.
correct_answer: Water droplets that condensed from vapor in the humid air.
explanation: When humid air touches a surface colder than its dew point, water vapor in that air condenses into liquid droplets. The cooled grass chills the air next to it, so dew forms on the blades. This is the condensation step of the water cycle.

distractor_rationales.choice: A dry surface, as the cool air draws water out of grass.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: cold air soaks up water; cooling air makes it hold less water vapor, so water condenses out of it

distractor_rationales.choice: Frost, because the grass drops below the freezing point of water.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: any surface cooler than the air freezes; with air near 18 °C, grass a few degrees colder stays far above 0 °C

distractor_rationales.choice: Raindrops from clouds too thin to see in the dark.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: dew falls from the sky like rain; the sky is clear, and dew forms on the surface from nearby air

real_world_check: Dew forms when a surface cools below the dew point of the air touching it, so water vapor in that air condenses into liquid droplets on the surface.

prompt: Rich deposits of copper ore are found in a few areas, while most land holds very little copper. Which statement best explains why copper ore is spread so unevenly?
choices: Long-ago geologic processes, like hot water in cracks, gathered copper in certain places.
Copper ore forms again within a few years in places where miners have dug it out.
People have already dug up the copper in other places, leaving ore in a few.
Copper ore grows larger each year in places that get more rain and snow.
correct_answer: Long-ago geologic processes, like hot water in cracks, gathered copper in certain places.
explanation: Metal ores form where geologic processes in the past concentrated the metal, for example hot fluids moving through cracks and leaving copper behind as they cooled. These conditions happened only in some places, so the ore is uneven.

distractor_rationales.choice: Copper ore forms again within a few years in places where miners have dug it out.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: mineral resources renew quickly; ore deposits take thousands to millions of years to form

distractor_rationales.choice: People have already dug up the copper in other places, leaving ore in a few.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: uneven resources are caused by human removal; the deposits were uneven before mining began

distractor_rationales.choice: Copper ore grows larger each year in places that get more rain and snow.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: ore grows like a living thing from rainfall; ore forms through slow geologic processes

real_world_check: Mineral resources are unevenly distributed because they formed only where past geologic processes, such as hydrothermal activity, concentrated them.

prompt: A body of granite formed deep underground. Over millions of years, uplift and erosion of the rock above it leave the granite exposed at the surface in a rainy climate. What will most likely happen to the exposed granite over time?

It will stay the same because granite is too hard to change.
It may turn into metamorphic rock because rain and cold air cool it quickly.
correct_answer: It will break down into grains that may later become sedimentary rock.
explanation: At the surface, rain, ice and chemical reactions break granite down into sand and clay. Water and wind carry these grains away, and when they are buried and pressed together they can become sedimentary rock, one path in the rock cycle.

distractor_rationales.choice: It will melt back into magma because sunlight heats the bare rock.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: sunlight can melt rock; melting needs the high temperatures found deep underground

distractor_rationales.choice: It will stay the same because granite is too hard to change.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: hard rocks are permanent; weathering slowly breaks down even granite at the surface

distractor_rationales.choice: It may turn into metamorphic rock because rain and cold air cool it quickly.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: rocks become metamorphic at the surface; metamorphism needs high heat and pressure underground

real_world_check: Rock exposed at Earth's surface is broken down by weathering, and the sediment is eroded, deposited and can be compacted and cemented into sedimentary rock.
